title: Going Ghost: Investigating the Lord Baltimore Hotel
excerpt: WBFF investigates reported paranormal activity and haunted history at Baltimore’s Lord Baltimore Hotel, documenting staff stories and on-site experiences.
content:
BALTIMORE (WBFF) — Strange happenings and whispered stories surround the Lord Baltimore Hotel, making it a magnet for guests hoping to encounter something paranormal.

The Lord Baltimore Hotel has a long, dark history that fuels its place among the most haunted hotels in America. Staff at the property often hear from guests about unusual experiences during their stay.

"It is not uncommon at all for us to get an email or a phone call or a comment from a guest saying they experienced something," said Lee Johnson-Lowe, Director of Marketing.

The team began its investigation at the speakeasy. Reports from this location describe classic haunting phenomena: echoes of lively parties, clinking glasses and distant singing. Vince, an investigator, explained that such tales are not unique. "

Well, it's a common haunting actually for speakeasies. It's the sounds of revelry, you know? Clinking glasses as people toast each other, singing and talking," said Vince Wilson, a paranormal expert.

On the 19th floor, the staff told WBFF about the story of an 8-year-old girl named Molly who is said to play with a red bouncy ball. Vince detailed the backstory behind the tale. "She was the daughter of a wealthy couple from upstate New York. They had lost everything in a stock market crash in 1929," he said.

The team found a secluded room on the same floor, not listed on the tour.

Reflecting on the visit, Vince said, "That's scary, regardless of whether or not it results in harm in any way. No one's ever been hurt here, but people certainly have experienced strange things."

Lee encourages guests to engage with the hotel's spirited reputation rather than shy away. "Don't be afraid of it, embrace it. They're all friendly here," Lee said.

The night closed with the team laughing nervously after a sudden unexpected noise, not sure if it was a ghost or just the old building settling.
